title: Residue cohomology interval on one specified perfect-model chart
statement: Let i:S→X be an immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme], A a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], I a maximal ideal, and U an object of S_proet [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sfbLocalRestriction, sfbCompletedModel and sfbResidueComplex from [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data], and actual inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let K lie in the derived category of modules over adicLisseCompletedRing X I. Fix a cochain complex P of finite projective A-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], zero in degrees below a and above b, and an isomorphism from sfbLocalRestriction i B U K to sfbLocalRestriction i B U (sfbCompletedModel X I P). Then for every q<a or b<q, the inverse image along i followed by restriction to the slice U of the underlying additive sheaf of H^q(Q.obj(sfbResidueComplex X I K)) is zero. The statement needs no global cover, stratification, compactness, completeness of A or K, or global boundedness conclusion.

proof.text: Apply proEtaleLocalScalarHomologyIso to the actual residue coefficient map and the specified isomorphism e. Exact fixed-scalar restriction retains the underlying additive sheaf and commutes with derived homology; the representative isomorphism in sfbResidueComplex identifies its homology with the scalar-extension homology. This identifies the two local residue cohomology sheaves.

proof.text: Projective A-module terms are flat. Identify the completed scalar-extension presentation with flatScalarRealization; its flatness theorem shows each term of the completed realization is flat. The realized complex is bounded above because its additive factors preserve zero terms. The independent-universe bounded-flat K-flat theorem therefore makes the derived reduction counit an isomorphism. No complete-reduction comparison or transport to a smaller site is required.

proof.text: For q<a or b<q, the qth term of P is zero. Constant realization and both ordinary scalar extensions preserve that zero term. The resulting qth homology is zero. Transport through the invertible K-flat computation counit, exact fixed-scalar restriction and its derived factorization. Apply additive inverse image and slice restriction, and transfer vanishing across the local residue-cohomology isomorphism from the first step.

theorem adicPerfectModel_localResidueBounds {X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : S ⟶ X)
    [IsImmersion i] {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.IsMaximal)
    (U : S.ProEt)
    (K : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules X (adicLisseCompletedRing X I)))
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    (ha : P.IsStrictlyGE a) (hb : P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hP : ∀ q : ℤ, Module.Projective A (P.X q) ∧ Module.Finite A (P.X q))
    (e : sfbLocalRestriction i (adicLisseCompletedRing X I) U K ≅
      sfbLocalRestriction i (adicLisseCompletedRing X I) U (sfbCompletedModel X I P)) :
    ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q →
      IsZero (((ProEt.topology S).overPullback AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U).obj
        ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage i AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
          ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
            (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (A ⧸ I ^ (0 + 1))) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj
                (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (sfbResidueComplex X I K))))))
